description: Scheduled Tasks page — manages recurring task execution. A task pairs an arbitrary task type (Workflow / Prompt / Auto-Fix / Watcher / Background-capture / Remote agent) with a schedule (cron / interval / once / condition). The page surfaces the task list, execution history with launch-failure and missed-runner-down indicators, and scheduler engine settings, plus a New Task form covering all variants and catch-up policy.

groups.name: Scheduler Status and Task Inventory
groups.description: Header with overall scheduler status (Running/Paused) and running-task count. Three sub-tabs (Scheduled / History / Settings) and an Auto-Fix shortcut. The Scheduled sub-tab shows the task inventory with per-task next-run, enable toggle, run-now, edit, and delete actions.

assertions.description: Users can identify the Scheduled Tasks page with a clear heading and see the scheduler's operational status (Running or Paused) along with the count of any currently executing tasks
Users can see whether the scheduler is currently running or paused through a visual status indicator, understanding at a glance whether scheduled tasks will execute on their configured schedules
Users can view summary statistics about scheduled task execution history, providing insight into execution patterns, success rates, and scheduling health

groups.name: Task Creation and Lifecycle
groups.description: Users can create new tasks via the New Task button, edit existing tasks, run them on-demand via Run Now, toggle their enabled state, or delete them. Each row in the task list shows: task name, task-type label (e.g. 'Workflow', 'Prompt', 'Remote agent'), schedule expression, next-run delta, and per-task action buttons. The Auto-Fix Now button at the top triggers the auto-fix run outside any schedule.

assertions.description: Users can create new scheduled tasks by clicking a New Task button, which opens a form for configuring the task name, task type variant, schedule definition, and execution parameters
Users can see all scheduled tasks in a list showing their names, schedules, associated task type, next run times, and enabled/disabled states, providing a complete inventory of recurring automation
Users can enable or disable individual scheduled tasks without deleting them, temporarily pausing specific recurring executions while keeping their configuration for future reactivation
Users can trigger the Auto-Fix mechanism immediately to run automated remediation outside the normal schedule, useful when errors are detected and immediate action is needed

groups.name: Execution History and Settings
groups.description: The History sub-tab shows the chronological log of executions per selected task. The Settings sub-tab exposes scheduler engine configuration (global enable, concurrency limits, etc).

assertions.description: Users can switch to the History sub-tab to review the chronological record of all scheduled task executions, understanding when tasks ran and whether they completed successfully
Users can switch to the Settings sub-tab to configure the scheduler engine parameters including global enable/disable, concurrency limits, and retry behavior
Users can refresh the scheduler data to see the latest task statuses, execution results, and updated next-run times without navigating away from the page

groups.name: Catch-up Policy Controls (Phase A/B/E)
groups.description: When a runner is offline at a task's scheduled fire time, the catch-up reconciler decides what to do. Users select per-task behavior via the 'If the runner was down' selector, with three options that map to the runner's CatchUpPolicy enum: 'run_once' (default — collapse all missed slots into one execution after the runner returns), 'run' (execute each missed slot individually), and 'skip' (record each missed slot as MissedRunnerDown without executing). A 'Grace window' input sets the seconds of slack — slots within `now - grace` of restart are considered fresh and not eligible for catch-up. The selector is only relevant for time-based schedules (Cron / Once / Interval); condition-based schedules don't have missed slots.

assertions.description: When the New Task form is open, a 'If the runner was down' select control with id 'catch-up-policy' is rendered. The select must have three options: 'Run once after returning' (value run_once, default), 'Run all missed slots' (value run), and 'Skip and log' (value skip).
assertions.precondition: New Task form is open and a time-based schedule (Cron / Once / Interval) is selected

assertions.description: A 'Grace window' numeric input with id 'catch-up-grace' is rendered alongside the catch-up policy selector. The default value is 300 (seconds). Slots within the grace window of the runner's restart time are treated as fresh and let the normal scheduler tick handle them, rather than triggering catch-up.
assertions.precondition: New Task form is open and a time-based schedule is selected

assertions.description: On a brand-new task form (no prefill), the catch-up policy selector's value reads as 'run_once'. This corresponds to the runner-side CatchUpPolicy::RunOnce default; if the rendered default drifts from the Rust default, persisted tasks will silently differ between the form and the runner.
assertions.precondition: New Task form is open with no prefill

assertions.description: When the schedule type is 'Condition', the catch-up policy selector is NOT rendered — condition-based schedules have no fire time and no concept of a missed slot. Showing the selector would be misleading.
assertions.precondition: New Task form is open and Condition schedule type is selected

groups.name: Remote Agent Task Type Form (Phase D/E)
groups.description: The 'Remote agent' task type lets users schedule arbitrary Claude prompts without pre-registering them in the prompt library. When this radio is selected the form reveals a multi-line prompt textarea, optional working directory, model selector, allowed-tools chip group, and an Advanced disclosure containing max-turns, timeout, and MCP-connection editor. At dispatch time the runner's launch_remote_agent calls POST /prompts/run with these fields. The form's defaults match the runner-side defaults (model = sonnet-4-6, allowed_tools = Bash/Read/Write/Edit/Glob/Grep, max_turns = 50, timeout = 600s); drift between form defaults and runner defaults causes silent behavior changes.

assertions.description: A 'Remote agent' radio option appears in the Task Type section of the New Task form alongside Workflow, Prompt, Auto-Fix, and the other variants. Selecting it switches the form to the RemoteAgent variant.

target.label: Remote agent task type radio label

assertions.description: A required prompt textarea with id 'agent-prompt' is rendered when Remote agent is selected. This is the actual prompt content that gets sent to /prompts/run. An empty prompt should disable the form's submit button (Create / Update).
assertions.precondition: Remote agent task type is selected

assertions.description: An optional 'Working directory' text input with id 'agent-working-directory' is rendered. If left blank the runner falls back to the project root; if set, it becomes the --working-directory flag on the spawned claude CLI.
assertions.precondition: Remote agent task type is selected

assertions.description: A 'Model' select with id 'agent-model' is rendered with at minimum claude-sonnet-4-6 (default), claude-opus-4-7, claude-haiku-4-5, and a '(custom)' sentinel that flips to a free-form input. The selected value becomes the --model flag on the claude CLI.
assertions.precondition: Remote agent task type is selected

assertions.description: An 'Allowed tools' chip group with id 'agent-allowed-tools' is rendered with role='group' and aria-labelledby='agent-allowed-tools-label'. Each chip is a checkbox with id 'agent-allowed-tool-<name>' (lowercase tool name) and aria-label 'Allowed tool: <Name>'. The visually-hidden underlying inputs make the chips fully UI-Bridge-discoverable. Default checked: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep. Optional: WebFetch, WebSearch, Task.
assertions.precondition: Remote agent task type is selected

assertions.description: The 'Bash' chip (id agent-allowed-tool-bash) is checked by default on a new task. If this drifts from the runner-side REMOTE_AGENT_DEFAULT_TOOLS array, scheduled remote-agent tasks will silently lose tool access.
assertions.precondition: Remote agent task type is selected on a new task with no prefill

assertions.description: Inside the Advanced disclosure: max-turns (id agent-max-turns, default 50), timeout (id agent-timeout, default 600), and an Add MCP connection button. These map to the runner's launch_remote_agent body's max_turns, timeout_seconds, and mcp_connections fields.
assertions.precondition: Remote agent task type is selected and the Advanced disclosure is expanded

groups.name: Launch Failure Backoff Display in Task List (Phase C/E)
groups.description: When a scheduled task's launch (start call) fails — e.g. workflow file missing, prompt-id not found, /prompts/run HTTP error, missing session_id — the runner increments task.consecutive_launch_failures and pushes next_run forward by min(base * 2^(failures-1), 86400) seconds. The task list surfaces this so the operator can see retries are being throttled. Required visual indicators: an orange 'launch_failed' badge on the task row, the next-run cell rendered as 'Next: in X (after N failures)' instead of plain 'Next: in X', and a tooltip explaining the wait. This is distinct from a runtime failure (status 'failed'), which doesn't push next_run forward — backoff applies only to LaunchFailed.

assertions.description: A task with consecutiveLaunchFailures > 0 displays a launch-failure badge in its task-row header. The badge text reads '<N> launch failure(s)' with correct singular/plural handling. The badge color is distinct from generic Failed (red) — uses the orange accent token to signal 'transient, will retry' instead of 'permanent failure'.
assertions.precondition: At least one task in the list has consecutiveLaunchFailures > 0

assertions.description: For a task with consecutiveLaunchFailures > 0, the next-run cell text contains the suffix '(after N failure(s))'. This suffix is the operator's signal that the displayed next_run is post-backoff, not the natural cron-derived next slot. If the suffix is absent on a backed-off task, the operator can't tell whether retries are actually deferred.
assertions.precondition: At least one task in the list has consecutiveLaunchFailures > 0

groups.name: History Status Badges for New Statuses (Phase B/E)
groups.description: The History sub-tab shows one row per execution. Beyond the original Pending/Running/Completed/Failed/Skipped/Cancelled, two new statuses landed in Phase B: 'launch_failed' (LaunchFailed — task could not start) and 'missed_runner_down' (MissedRunnerDown — slot was synthesized by the catch-up reconciler with policy=Skip). These need distinguishable visual treatment because they mean different things from generic Failed: launch_failed is retry-with-backoff, missed_runner_down is informational. Catch-up runs also tag the task name with '(catch-up)' so the operator can tell that a Completed row was a catch-up rather than a normal-schedule fire.

assertions.description: Records with status='launch_failed' render a badge with text 'Launch failed' (not generic 'Failed'). The badge uses the orange accent token. Showing them as plain Failed would mislead the operator into treating transient launch errors as permanent.
assertions.precondition: History tab is selected and at least one execution record has status=launch_failed

assertions.description: Records with status='missed_runner_down' render a badge with text 'Missed (runner offline)'. The badge uses the slate (neutral cool-gray) accent. These records are synthesized by the reconciler when catch_up_policy=Skip — they have started_at == ended_at == reconcile-time and represent slots that were not actually executed.
assertions.precondition: History tab is selected and at least one execution record has status=missed_runner_down

assertions.description: Records with catchUpRun=true render the task name suffixed with ' (catch-up)'. This applies regardless of final status (Completed, Failed, MissedRunnerDown all may be catch-up runs). Without the suffix, an operator cannot tell from the History tab alone whether a row was a normal-schedule execution or a reconciler-synthesized one.
assertions.precondition: History tab is selected and at least one execution record has catchUpRun=true

assertions.description: Records with a populated scheduledFor field show a 'Scheduled for: <ts>, ran: <ts>' tooltip on the row and a visible 'Scheduled for: <ts>' line in the metadata block. The two timestamps make 'ran X minutes late' inspectable — for normal runs the values are close; for catch-up runs scheduledFor will be far earlier than startedAt. Records without scheduledFor (legacy rows pre-migration) must NOT crash the row; they simply omit this metadata.
assertions.precondition: History tab is selected and at least one record has scheduledFor populated

groups.name: Visual Design and Theme Compliance
groups.description: Style-guide coverage: scheduler tab uses the runner's standard panel layout with semantic accent colors for status indicators. Critical theme tokens: orange for transient/retry states (launch_failed, launch-failure backoff badge), slate for neutral/informational (missed_runner_down), red for permanent failures (failed), green for completed, blue for running, yellow for pending/skipped. These accent semantics MUST stay consistent across the task list, history rows, and any new surface that displays task state, otherwise operators will misread severity.

assertions.description: The 'Launch failed' history badge and the launch-failure list badge both use the orange accent token (text-orange-500 / bg-orange-500/10 in the runner's design system). Distinct from red Failed; signals 'transient — system will retry'.
assertions.precondition: History tab is selected and at least one record has status=launch_failed

assertions.description: The 'Missed (runner offline)' badge uses the slate (neutral cool-gray) accent. Visually de-emphasized vs Completed/Failed because the slot was never executed — it's an audit trail, not an outcome.
assertions.precondition: History tab is selected and at least one record has status=missed_runner_down

states.name: Scheduled Tasks List
states.description: The Scheduled sub-tab is active showing the inventory of scheduled tasks with per-task toggles, the Auto-Fix Now button, and the New Task creation button. The header displays overall scheduler status (Running/Paused) and running task count.

states.name: Execution History
states.description: The History sub-tab is active showing a chronological log of scheduled task executions with task names, timestamps, durations, and success/failure outcomes. Status badges include the new launch_failed (orange) and missed_runner_down (slate) variants; rows where catchUpRun=true show a '(catch-up)' suffix.

states.name: Scheduler Settings
states.description: The Settings sub-tab is active showing scheduler engine configuration options including global enable/disable, concurrency limits, and retry policies.

states.name: New Task Form
states.description: The task creation form is open. Always shows the Task name input, schedule controls, the catch-up policy selector (id catch-up-policy) for time-based schedules, and the Task Type radio group (Workflow / Prompt / Auto-Fix / Watcher / Background-capture / Remote agent). Selecting Remote agent reveals the agent-prompt textarea, model select, allowed-tools chip group, and Advanced disclosure. Cancel and Create (or Update when editing) buttons are at the bottom.

transitions.name: Cancel and return to task list
Save new task and return to list
Switch task type to Remote agent

states.name: New Task Form — Remote Agent variant
states.description: Sub-state of the New Task form: the Remote agent task type is selected, revealing the prompt textarea (id agent-prompt), working-directory input, model select, allowed-tools chip group (id agent-allowed-tools with chip ids agent-allowed-tool-{bash,read,write,edit,glob,grep,webfetch,websearch,task}), and an Advanced disclosure containing max-turns / timeout / MCP connections.

states.name: New Task Form — Remote Agent Advanced fields
states.description: Sub-state of the Remote-agent variant: the Advanced disclosure is expanded, exposing max-turns (id agent-max-turns, default 50), timeout (id agent-timeout, default 600), and the Add MCP connection button. These map to the runner's launch_remote_agent body fields max_turns, timeout_seconds, and mcp_connections.
